docs.title: HyFI: Hydra Fast Interface
docs.text:
HyFI composes Hydra configs, validates them with Pydantic, and runs reproducible workflows. Every run writes a manifest with the resolved config, the code version, and per-step results, so the same run can be repeated later, by a person or by a coding agent.

  • Documentation
  • Migrating from 1.x

HyFI 2.0 is a rewrite. The 1.x line stays on the v1 branch; pin hyfi<2 to keep it.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
uv add hyfi          # or: pip install hyfi
uvx hyfi --version   # run without installing

Python 3.11 or newer. Core dependencies: hydra-core, omegaconf, pydantic, python-dotenv.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Put configs in ./conf:

# conf/workflow/charcount.yaml
name: charcount
steps:
  - run: pathlib.Path
    with: {_args_: [README.md]}
  - run: pathlib.Path.read_text   # receives the previous result as its first argument
  - run: builtins.len

hyfi run workflow=charcount --dry-run   # resolve every step without running it
hyfi run workflow=charcount             # run it and write .hyfi/runs/<run_id>/manifest.json
hyfi rerun <run_id>                     # run the recorded config again

From Python or a notebook:

import hyfi

cfg = hyfi.compose(["workflow=charcount"])
manifest = hyfi.run_workflow(cfg)
print(manifest.status, [s.status for s in manifest.steps])

docs.title: What is in the box
docs.text:
• compose() / instantiate() / BaseConfig: Hydra composition with Pydantic validation, from the CLI, code, or notebooks. Nothing happens at import time.
  • Plugins: any package can ship config groups through the hyfi.plugins entry point.
  • Workflows: ordered steps, each a Python callable built with Hydra instantiate; results pipe into the next step.
  • Run manifests: resolved config, git SHA, uv.lock hash, Python and platform, timings, errors.
  • Execution allowlist: --allow 'mypkg.*' limits which callables a config may run (forwarded to Hydra 1.4's execution whitelist).
  • Agent-friendly CLI: --json on every command, hyfi config schema for JSON Schema, non-zero exit codes on failure.

docs.title: Using HyFI from coding agents
docs.text:
Every command takes --json and exits non-zero on failure (1: the run or check failed, 2: usage or config error, with {"error": ...} on stdout when --json is given).

A safe loop for an agent:

  1. Inspect: hyfi plugins --json, hyfi config show workflow=<name> --json.
  2. Learn the shape: hyfi config schema workflow (or project, or any dotted Pydantic model) prints JSON Schema.
  3. Dry-run with an allowlist: hyfi run workflow=<name> --dry-run --json --allow '<pkg>.*'. Every step must report "ok": true.
  4. Run: same command without --dry-run. Read status and steps[*].status from the JSON output.
  5. Reproduce: hyfi rerun <run_id> --json; the manifest is at <project.root>/.hyfi/runs/<run_id>/manifest.json.

Manifests, hyfi run output, and dry-run plans replace the value of every ${oc.env:...} variable (4+ characters) with its interpolation, so they carry no secrets. hyfi config show resolves everything; use --no-resolve before sharing its output.

Always pass --allow when the config was written or changed by someone other than the person who asked for the run.

docs.title: API reference
docs.text:
Compose Hydra configs and validate them with Pydantic.

Nothing here runs at import time: no resolvers, no global Hydra state, no environment changes.

Workflows: an ordered list of steps, each a callable built with Hydra instantiate.

.. code-block:: yaml

# conf/workflow/demo.yaml
name: demo
steps:
  - run: mypkg.io.load_csv
    with: {path: data/in.csv}
  - run: mypkg.clean.clean      # gets the previous result as its first argument
  - run: mypkg.io.save
    with: {path: out.csv}
    pipe: true

Run the workflow node of a composed config and record a manifest.

Run manifests: what ran, with which resolved config, on which code, and how it went.

Project paths, validated from the composed project node.

Discover plugin config modules through the hyfi.plugins entry point group.

A plugin declares, in its own pyproject.toml::

[project.entry-points."hyfi.plugins"]
mypkg = "mypkg.conf"

The value is an importable package that holds Hydra config groups.

docs.text: Every _target_ (string or callable) in a nested config of dicts, lists, and tuples.

docs.title: resolve_config_dir(config_dir)
docs.text: The user config directory: the given one (which must exist), else ./conf if present.

docs.title: search_path(config_dir=None, config_name=DEFAULT_CONFIG_NAME, plugins=True)
docs.text:
Return the primary config source and the extra search-path entries, highest priority first.

The user directory is primary when it holds <config_name>.yaml; otherwise hyfi._primary (which holds only config.yaml) is, and the user directory comes first among the extras. HyFI's own groups are always last, so group options resolve user > plugins > HyFI in both cases.

docs.title: compose(overrides=(), *, config_name=DEFAULT_CONFIG_NAME, config_dir=None, plugins=True, dotenv=True)
docs.text:
Compose a config the way the hyfi CLI does, from code or a notebook.

dotenv loads the nearest .env (without overriding variables already set) before composing, so ${oc.env:...} interpolations can see it.

docs.title: compose_group(group, name, overrides=(), **compose_kwargs)
docs.text: Compose one option of a config group and return just that node.

docs.title: to_dict(cfg, resolve=True)
docs.text: Plain Python containers from a DictConfig, ListConfig, or Pydantic model.

docs.title: instantiate(config, *args, allow=None, **kwargs)
docs.text:
hydra.utils.instantiate that also accepts Pydantic models and passes plain containers.

A Pydantic model as _target_ is validated by its own constructor. allow is an execution allowlist (exact targets or pkg.*): every nested _target_ must match it, and it is forwarded to Hydra's _execution_whitelist_ on Hydra 1.4+.

docs.title: plan(workflow, allow=None)
docs.text:
Resolve every step target without calling it.

ok is False when a target cannot be imported or, with allow, is outside the allowlist.

docs.title: execute(workflow, on_record=None, allow=None)
docs.text:
Run the steps in order and return the last result and one record per step.

With pipe (the default) a step receives the previous step's result as its first positional argument when that result is not None. On failure the remaining steps are marked skipped and :class:WorkflowError carries the records. allow is the execution allowlist passed to :func:hyfi.config.instantiate.

docs.title: env_replacements(raw)
docs.text: Map the current value of every env var named in an oc.env: reference to its interpolation.

docs.title: redact(obj, replacements)
docs.text: Replace every occurrence of a secret value in every string (keys included) of obj.

docs.title: keep_env_interpolations(resolved, raw)
docs.text:
resolved, except leaves whose unresolved form reads ${oc.env:...} stay unresolved.

Values from the environment (often secrets) are re-read on rerun instead of being recorded.

docs.title: record_config(config)
docs.text:
Return (resolved, recorded, replacements) for a composed or recorded config.

resolved is what runs. recorded is the config view written to manifests and printed: ${oc.env:...} leaves stay unresolved and every env value from replacements is replaced by its interpolation. project.root / project.workspace are made absolute before resolving, in both views, so values that interpolate them are absolute as well. Callers apply :func:redact with replacements to anything else they emit (names, errors).

docs.title: load_workflow(config)
docs.text: Validate the project and workflow nodes of a composed (or recorded) config.

docs.title: run_workflow(config, *, overrides=(), config_name=None, config_dir=None, argv=(), rerun_of=None, allow=None)
docs.text:
Execute the workflow and write <project.root>/.hyfi/runs/<run_id>/manifest.json.

The manifest is written before the first step and again at the end, so a crash leaves a running record. Step failures are recorded, not raised; check manifest.status. allow is the execution allowlist (see :func:hyfi.config.instantiate).

docs.title: Migrating from 1.x
docs.text:
HyFI 2.0 is a rewrite with a much smaller core. There is no compatibility layer.

Staying on 1.x: pin hyfi<2 (projects generated from hyfi-template already pin ^1.36). The 1.x source lives on the v1 branch. HyFI 1.x does not install on Python 3.13 or newer.

1.x 2.0 from hyfi import HyFI, HyFI.compose(...) hyfi.compose([...overrides]) HyFI.instantiate(cfg), instantiate_config hyfi.instantiate(cfg) hyfi.composer.BaseConfig with implicit composition on construction hyfi.BaseConfig subclass, explicit Model.compose() hyfi.composer.BaseModel, Field, validators pydantic directly HyFI.initialize_global_hyfi(plugins=[...]) [project.entry-points."hyfi.plugins"] in pyproject.toml hyfi_main() CLI wrapper the hyfi CLI (config, plugins, run, rerun) workflow → task → pipeline → pipe, uses: workflow with a flat steps: list, run: + with: Runner, BatchTask, /batch, /path:__batch__ Project paths plus run manifests built-in /pipe dataframe and dataset helpers, jsonl/dataframe I/O, graphics removed: call pandas, datasets, or your own functions as steps about 30 custom resolvers (__get_path__, today, iif, ...) interpolation of composed values (${project.root}) and Hydra's built-ins (${now:...}, ${oc.env:...}) hyfi-run click CLI, copier commands removed

A 1.x pipeline such as

steps:
  - uses: load_dataframes
    with: {data_files: in.parquet}
  - uses: save_dataframes
    with: {data_file: out.parquet}

becomes

steps:
  - run: pandas.read_parquet
    with: {path: in.parquet}
  - run: pandas.DataFrame.to_parquet
    with: {path: out.parquet}

docs.title: Writing a plugin
docs.text:
A plugin is an ordinary Python package that ships Hydra config groups. Declare the config package in pyproject.toml:

[project]
name = "mypkg"
dependencies = ["hyfi>=2"]

[project.entry-points."hyfi.plugins"]
mypkg = "mypkg.conf"

src/mypkg/
  __init__.py
  steps.py
  conf/
    __init__.py
    workflow/
      tokenize.yaml
    tokenizer/
      simple.yaml

After uv add mypkg, its groups are available everywhere HyFI composes:

hyfi plugins               # name, module, distribution, importable?
hyfi run workflow=tokenize

Guidelines:

  • Keep the library usable without HyFI; put HyFI-specific wiring in conf/ and small step functions.
  • Name group options so they do not collide with other plugins. When two sources define the same option, the user directory wins, then plugins in name order, then HyFI.
  • Use hyfi.BaseConfig for typed defaults that live in your config groups.

docs.title: Configs
docs.text:
HyFI looks for configs in three places, highest priority first:

  1. Your config directory: --config-dir, or ./conf when it exists.
  2. Installed plugins (the hyfi.plugins entry point group), in name order.
  3. HyFI's own defaults (hyfi.conf): a project group and an empty workflow slot.

This order holds whether or not your directory has its own config.yaml.

If your directory holds config.yaml it becomes the primary config. Start it from HyFI's defaults:

# conf/config.yaml
defaults:
  - project: default
  - workflow: null
  - _self_

Select group options and change values with ordinary Hydra overrides (except hydra.searchpath, which HyFI sets itself; add directories with --config-dir or a plugin instead):

hyfi config show workflow=charcount project.name=demo
hyfi config show --json --no-resolve

.env in the current directory (or a parent) is loaded before composing, without overriding variables that are already set, so ${oc.env:NAME,default} can read it.

docs.title: Project
docs.text:
The project node becomes a hyfi.Project:

key default env name hyfi-project HYFI_PROJECT_NAME root . HYFI_PROJECT_ROOT workspace <root>/workspace (${project.workspace} in configs) HYFI_PROJECT_WORKSPACE

Run manifests go to <root>/.hyfi/runs/.

docs.title: Workflows
docs.text:
A workflow is a list of steps. Each step names a callable in run and its keyword arguments in with. Hydra builds it with instantiate, so nested _target_ values inside with are built too, and _args_ gives positional arguments.

name: clean
steps:
  - run: mypkg.io.load_csv
    with: {path: data/in.csv}
  - run: mypkg.text.normalize     # gets the loaded table as its first argument
    with: {lowercase: true}
  - run: mypkg.io.save_csv
    with: {path: "${project.workspace}/out.csv"}
  • pipe: true (default) passes the previous step's result as the first positional argument when it is not None. Set pipe: false to start fresh.
  • A step's name defaults to the last part of run.
  • A failing step stops the run; later steps are recorded as skipped.

Your own modules must be importable: run HyFI inside your project's environment (uv run hyfi ... after declaring your package), or use python -m hyfi, which puts the current directory on sys.path.

docs.title: Runs and reruns
docs.text:
hyfi run workflow=clean                 # exit 0 on success, 1 if a step failed
hyfi run workflow=clean --dry-run       # resolve targets only; exit 1 if any cannot be imported
hyfi rerun 20261019T010203Z-a1b2c3      # run the recorded resolved config again

The manifest records the run id, status, start and end time, HyFI and Python versions, platform, argv, config name and directory, overrides, the allowlist, the fully resolved config, git SHA and dirty flag, the SHA-256 of uv.lock, and per-step status, seconds, and error.

The manifest stores the resolved config with environment values taken out. HyFI collects every variable your config names in ${oc.env:NAME} and, wherever its current value appears in a manifest, hyfi run output, or a dry-run plan (config values, aliases such as ${secret}, step names, error messages), writes ${oc.env:NAME} instead. A rerun reads the environment again; if it changed, the rerun sees the new value. Values shorter than 4 characters are not redacted, so keep secrets out of short variables. Project root and workspace are recorded as absolute paths (unless they came from the environment), so a rerun writes to the original project even when started elsewhere.

hyfi rerun does not recompose: it executes the recorded config, so interpolations such as ${now:...} keep their recorded values.

docs.title: Execution allowlist
docs.text:
A config decides which Python callables run. When configs come from somewhere you do not fully trust, limit them:

hyfi run workflow=clean --allow 'mypkg.*' --allow builtins.len
HYFI_ALLOW='mypkg.*,builtins.len' hyfi run workflow=clean

A pattern is an exact target or pkg.* for everything under a package. Every _target_ in a step, including nested ones (in mappings, lists, or tuples, as strings or callables), must match; from Python, hyfi.instantiate(..., allow=...) also checks targets passed as call-site arguments. On Hydra 1.4+ the list is also passed to Hydra's execution whitelist. hyfi rerun reuses the recorded list unless you pass --allow. Without a list, Hydra's default applies (Hydra 1.4 warns; 1.5 plans to refuse).

docs.title: Typed config groups
docs.text:
from hyfi import BaseConfig


class Tokenizer(BaseConfig):
    _config_group_ = "tokenizer"
    _config_name_ = "simple"
    lowercase: bool = True


tok = Tokenizer.compose(overrides=["tokenizer.lowercase=false"])

compose() composes tokenizer=simple with the usual search path and validates the node.
